interactions:
DRUG REVIEW — COMBINED OCP IN MIGRAINE WITH AURA

Query: Ethinylestradiol + drospirenone combined oral contraceptive in a woman with migraine with visual and sensory aura

FINDINGS: WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria Category 4 = UNACCEPTABLE RISK.
Migraine with aura + combined OCP: approximately 6-9-fold increased ischaemic stroke risk compared to women with neither. All combined hormonal contraceptives (combined OCP, combined patch, combined vaginal ring) are Category 4 in migraine with aura.

SAFE ALTERNATIVES: Desogestrel-only pill (Cerazette 75 mcg daily): WHO Category 2. Levonorgestrel IUD: Category 2. Copper IUD: Category 1. Etonogestrel implant: Category 2.

CONCLUSION: Combined OCP is WHO Category 4 — contraindicated in migraine with aura; progestin-only and non-hormonal alternatives are WHO Category 1-2.

results.abstract:
LITERATURE SEARCH: Migraine Aura — Combined Visual and Sensory Symptoms

KEY FINDINGS:
1. MULTIPLE AURA SYMPTOMS: Up to 30% of patients with migraine with aura have >1 aura type in a single episode (visual + sensory is most common combination)
2. SEQUENTIAL SPREAD: Combined visual-sensory aura often presents as visual symptoms first, then sensory spreading as CSD crosses from occipital to parietal cortex
3. ICHD-3 CRITERIA: Still met with combination aura — each symptom meets duration and spreading criteria
4. CAUTION: Combined visual + sensory aura with headache has a wider differential than visual-only aura, especially in patients with vascular risk factors
5. NEGATIVE SENSORY (NUMBNESS): Negative sensory symptoms (numbness without tingling) can occur in migraine aura, contrary to the classic teaching that only TIA causes negative symptoms

CONCLUSION: Combined visual and sensory aura is a recognised migraine variant. Thorough secondary cause exclusion is required especially in young women on combined OCP.
results.title: Literature review

output.summary: Combined visual and sensory aura is seen in approximately 30% of migraine with aura episodes; negative sensory symptoms (numbness) can occur in migraine aura;

results.abstract:
LITERATURE SEARCH: Migraine, Stroke Risk, and Ethnicity

KEY FINDINGS:
1. BLACK WOMEN AND STROKE: Black women have 2-3x higher ischaemic stroke risk than White women at reproductive age; reasons include higher hypertension rates, sickle cell trait, lupus anticoagulant
2. MIGRAINE WITH AURA + OCP: Risk applies across ethnicities; combined hormonal contraceptives are WHO Category 4 in migraine with aura regardless of ethnicity
3. FAMILY HISTORY OF EARLY-ONSET STROKE: Young-onset stroke in a first-degree relative is a recognised vascular risk factor warranting lipid and blood pressure monitoring
4. THROMBOPHILIA SCREENING: Recommended in young patients with stroke or TIA; negative results exclude an acquired hypercoagulable state
5. SICKLE CELL TRAIT: Can cause stroke via sickling in cerebral vessels; excluded by haemoglobin electrophoresis

Clinical correlation recommended.
results.title: Literature review

patient.history_present_illness:
A 29-year-old Nigerian-British woman presented to the neurology outpatient clinic with two episodes over the past 6 weeks of a similar disturbance. In both episodes, she first noticed a shimmering, flickering area in the left side of her visual field that slowly expanded over approximately 15-20 minutes. Simultaneously with the second half of the visual disturbance, she noticed numbness of her left hand and left cheek — a 'dead' feeling without tingling. Both symptoms resolved completely within 30 minutes and were followed by a severe right-sided pulsating headache (8/10) with nausea, vomiting, and severe photophobia lasting 12-14 hours.

She had never experienced anything like this before the first episode 6 weeks ago. She mentioned to her GP that she had visited Nigeria 8 weeks ago, where the weather was very hot — this was two weeks before the first episode. She has no cardiac disease, no hypertension, and no family history of stroke. Her mother never mentioned migraines but 'always had bad headaches'. She is currently on the combined oral contraceptive pill (Yasmin — EE 30 mcg + drospirenone) and has been for 3 years. She is a junior doctor in her first year of training, and the episodes both occurred during very stressful on-call periods.

She is particularly concerned because her father had a stroke at age 45. She is a non-smoker, no alcohol. She is otherwise very healthy. She specifically denies any weakness, speech difficulty, or any persisting visual loss.
